title.narrative: WFP Emergency Unconditional Cash Assistance for Sudanese Crisis-Affected Population

description.narrative: As a result of the recent Sudan crisis, hundreds of thousands of Sudanese citizens are fleeing their country and seeking refuge in Egypt. Food Security Outcome Monitoring (FSOM) conducted in September 2024 revealed a decline in food security among newly arrived Sudanese households, with 49% reporting inadequate food consumption. The deterioration in food security is attributed to inflationary pressures and the limited capacity of households to cope with escalating food prices, fear of deportation or detention due to lack of residency permit and legal documents led to movement restrictions, limiting access to food. In line with increasing food insecurity, and lack of assistance due to limited funding, many households resorted to extensive negative coping strategies. Most of the households rely on less preferred or less expensive food or reducing the number of meals per day. Over 48% of surveyed households were severely relying on food-related coping strategies. To address food security challenges among Sudanese newcomers, WFP plans to provide emergency monthly cash assistance to 40,000 people over the period of 3 months. Each person will receive USD 14.8 per month through e-cards. The intervention is designed to respond to the immediate food needs of Sudanese newcomers who entered Egypt as a result of the crisis erupted in April 2023. Through this emergency response, WFP aims to address the food security sector, ensuring that food insecure Sudanese crisis-affected new arrivals in Egypt have access to adequate food. This assistance leverages existing cash delivery modality under the General Food Assistance programme, WFP’s flagship initiative, and is supported by the robust partnership with Fawry, a leading financial service provider (FSP) which has more than 140,000 points of sale nationwide. The cash assistance programme was developed based on consultations with affected populations, community leaders, community-based organizations (CBOs), and NGOs. WFP will utilize its online enrollment tool to allow affected individuals to self-enroll. Using the collected data, WFP will apply food security vulnerability-based targeting criteria to identify the most vulnerable individuals, particularly those who are not receiving any other form of assistance. This life-saving assistance is especially critical for individuals awaiting appointments to be registered as refugees under UNHCR. This group is particularly vulnerable, as their non-refugee status excludes them from accessing other available assistance and services. Additionally, their insecure legal status heightens the risk of deportation and detention. Crisis-affected Sudanese residing in Upper Egypt, such as Aswan and Luxor, face further challenges due to the significant distance to registration sites. Traveling to these sites not only poses logistical difficulties but also increases the risk of deportation and detention. WFP’s monthly emergency cash assistance will significantly help Sudanese newcomers cope with food insecurity. Evidence shows that 80% of WFP’s monthly cash assistance is used to purchase food.
